title: LLM Misuse Safeguards Rely on Untrusted Input: A Widespread, High-Risk Vulnerability
abstract: arXiv:2607.27951v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language models now help professionals in fields such as cybersecurity and biology, yet the same answers would help an attacker. Deployers rely on misuse safeguards to keep such answers from attackers. We find that these safeguards share a high-risk vulnerability: they decide whether to release an answer from what users write, including the professional identity or purpose they claim, and anyone can write such a claim. Threat reports from model vendors and security firms show that attackers who fabricate a professional identity or purpose already exploit this vulnerability to cause serious harm. The vulnerability is also widespread across the state of the art: every defense proposed in 129 papers from the latest editions of 12 top venues has it. translated_title: 大型语言模型滥用防护措施依赖不可信输入：一种广泛存在的高风险漏洞
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型如今在网络安全和生物学等领域为专业人士提供帮助，然而同样的答案也会为攻击者所用。部署方依赖滥用防护措施来防止此类答案落入攻击者手中。我们发现这些防护措施存在一个共同的高风险漏洞：它们根据用户所写的内容来决定是否发布答案，包括用户声称的专业身份或用途，而任何人都可以编写此类声明。来自模型厂商和安全公司的威胁报告显示，伪造专业身份或用途的攻击者已经在利用这一漏洞造成严重危害。该漏洞在当前最先进的技术中也普遍存在：来自12个顶级会议最新一届的129篇论文中所提出的每一项防御措施都存在此漏洞。防护措施研究的研究对象出了错：它将危害视为请求文本本身的属性，尽管相同的文本可能来自专业人士，也可能来自攻击者。目前的防护……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 大型语言模型的滥用防护措施因依赖用户自述的身份或用途等不可信输入来决定是否放行答案，存在被攻击者通过伪造声明绕过的高风险漏洞，且该漏洞普遍存在于12个顶级会议129篇论文所提出的全部防御方案中。
en_tdlr: LLM misuse safeguards rely on untrusted user-written claims (such as claimed professional identity or purpose) to decide whether to release answers, creating a widespread, high-risk vulnerability already exploited by attackers and present in every defense proposed across 129 papers from 12 top venues.
